newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Tuesday on profit-taking triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
LME copper fell prey to general liquidation during afternoon kerb trading on Monday on rising stocks. Final business was at $2,353, below its high of $2,386 and Friday's close of $2,374.

The most actively traded local red metal November 1997 contract ended at 21,280 yuan ($2,567) per tonne, losing 140 yuan. It opened at 21,220 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 21,200 yuan and a high of 21,540 yuan per tonne.
August rose 50 to 20,950 yuan per tonne, September fell 90 to 21,030, October 140 to 21,250, December 200 to 21,300 and the January 1997 contract 200 to 21,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 101,480 tonnes from 177,150 tonnes.
Copper opened lower but rose steadily on speculative buying and short-covering at low levels before profit-taking pushed prices off highs.
Traders said overnight LME losses prompted many Shanghai investors to take profit at high levels on Tuesday.
"Some wary investors continued to liquidate their long positions today due to heavy gains over the past few days," one trader said.
"But volume was thinner than Monday, indicating many institutional buyers are still optimistic about the later market trend," he added.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices fell to around 20,900 yuan per tonne, compared with 21,000 on Monday after solid gains over the past few trading days.
Traders said the market was quiet after two days of technical corrections but fluctuations were expected in the next few days with heavy speculative hot money flowing into the market.
Aluminium ended mostly down. August fell 80 to 13,950 yuan per tonne, September 120 to 14,220, October was unchanged at 14,380, November dropped 50 to 14,300 and December 50 to 14,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 2,610 tonnes from 4,890 tonnes.
